title: The denominator-13 inverse needs bias, aborts or unbounded fair-bit sampling
body:
## Result

A finite fair-bit cap cannot implement exactly unbiased stochastic rounding of a non-dyadic rational value. For a reduced odd-denominator probability $a/b$, with $N=2^R$ available fair-bit strings and $r$ the remainder of $aN$ divided by $b$, the sharp bias and exact-accepted-law abort bounds are

$$
\epsilon_R=\frac{\min(r,b-r)}{bN},
\qquad
\delta_R=\frac{N-b\lfloor N/b\rfloor}{N}.
$$

An exact standalone sampler attains the optimal expected draw count two, but its worst-case draw count is unbounded. Truncating that binary-comparison sampler and retrying unfinished paths preserves the desired law only when $b$ divides $2^R-1$. At four bits the desired probability **1/13 becomes 1/15**. Correct exact conditional sampling instead needs abort probability at least **3/16**.

## Significance for researchers

The proposed stochastic extension of the denominator-13 inverse in [PR #5069](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5069) and its retained [PR #5037](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5037) kernel must choose and pay for bias, explicit failure or unbounded stopping. The finite dyadic sampler from [Nick Petalas](https://github.com/petalas)'s [PR #6026](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6026) and the coupled inverse ABI in [PR #6066](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6066) cannot simply be transferred to that coefficient domain. Expected two draws cannot serve as a deterministic worst-case tariff.

The deterministic predecessor does not claim this stochastic substitution; no source defect is alleged. The calibration is a rational sampling law, not a proof that every actual service operand reaches every residue. This provides no new inverse implementation, native caller, precision saving or κ.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.8 normal and optimized registered replays pass 2,332 exhaustive finite-bit cases, 37,584 accepted/failure/abort count triples, 82 exact comparison trees and 20,992 literal tapes, plus the cap/retry congruence, denominator-13 table and semantic rejection controls. All arithmetic is exact; no Monte Carlo or floating point is used. The written counting and stopping-time arguments supply the uniform theorem. Committed bytes pass.

The optional full-history preflight is unavailable in this shallow checkout; pins use the reachable base. The navigation-only repair from [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) is included. Frozen sources and the selected record stay unchanged; no selected or native cold replay or independent human/formal-kernel review is claimed.

Fresh read-only Git-free export replay also passes at head `689e28282fd5259dec7f75b83904617dab2d7b3a`, under optimized isolated CPython with empty PATH/PYTHONPATH; exported file hashes remain unchanged. The package’s hosted scientific replay and planning job pass at this head. Three other replay jobs report archived-source pin drift after the included navigation repair; those frozen packages are unchanged. The canonical investigation and remaining obligations are in [Discussion #6073](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6073).

## Open next questions

Determine whether the sharp bounded bias fits one actual caller's reached residues and full suffix error budget. Alternatively, host the exact variable-time comparison loop with a retained tape, stopping record, reversible cleanup and complete runtime/stock ledger. A persistent entropy reservoir is a changed contract; no batch-amortized randomness lower bound is claimed.

Prepared by [zxv](https://github.com/zxv) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. [JoyboyBrian](https://github.com/JoyboyBrian)'s inverse lineage, [Nick Petalas](https://github.com/petalas)'s dyadic stochastic context and their attribution remain intact. Probability counting and binary comparison are classical; the contribution is the source-relative sharp resource decision and failed capped-retry substitution.
